it_load_citation: [inference] SCREENING bracket — NOT a disclosure. A DISCLOSED LOAD FIGURE NOW EXISTS AND IS DELIBERATELY NOT ADOPTED HERE (#1469): PJM's TEAC Dayton Supplemental filing of 2026-07-07 carries M-3 Need Dayton-2025-002, 'AES Ohio has a customer request for service in the vicinity of its Clinton Substation near Wilmington, OH', ramping 35 MW (1/2028) -> 100 MW (4/2028) -> 300 MW (1/2029) -> 500 MW (1/2030). It is not adopted for three reasons, each sufficient: (a) it is TOTAL REQUESTED NEW LOAD at a delivery point — facility demand, not IT load (read back through this repo's own PUE band 1.13-1.45 it implies ~345-442 MW of IT, which lands inside the bracket below and under its 480.1 high, so the two methods AGREE rather than conflict); (b) it is a request with a 2030 terminal year, not installed capacity; and (c) decisively, THE FILING NAMES A SUBSTATION AND A CITY, NEVER A CUSTOMER — the Clinton Substation parcel is 53 m from the nearest Ardent/TAC petitioned-rezoning tract and 1.03 mi from the nearest AWS-owned Cosler Farm holding, so the 500 MW cannot be assigned to this campus on the present record (the Van Wert #1408 shape: an instrument that documents the load but not the customer does not lift the facility). Records: data/extracted/grid/wilmington/clinton-delivery-point.interconnection.yaml, data/extracted/wilmington/power-watch.yaml. Primary basis = the network floor-area screen (cf. Urbana #1327 / Troy-Piqua): the disclosed 9-building site plan's 1,920,299 sq ft gross floor area (Nov/Dec 2025) x a whole-building IT power-density band of 75-250 W/sq ft (stated screening assumption) -> 144.0 MW low, ~312 MW central (MW-midpoint; watermark.facility.screening — #1641 D2), 480.1 MW high. Corroborated (not a second source) by the investment screen (cf. Sidney): the [reported] $4B campus / a hyperscale ~$8.5-20M-per-MW-IT construction-cost band -> ~200 MW ($20M/MW) .. ~470 MW ($8.5M/MW) — the two independent screens agree at an order-of-magnitude ~150-480 MW, so the bracket is set there (central ~312 MW). Signals that point HIGHER but are NOT adopted into the bracket: (a) the 9->12-building revision tabled 2026-03-27 is unreconciled [open] and would scale the floor area up; (b) the [reported] 252 Tier-4 diesel gensets, at a typical hyperscale per-unit rating (undisclosed), imply a larger N+1 backup envelope. RETIRED signal: the widely repeated '1.5 GW' is NOT this campus's figure at all and must not be carried as one — #1469 traced it to the SAME PJM deck's PREVIOUS slide, Need Dayton-2025-001, 'in the vicinity of its Fayette Substation in Jeffersonville, OH' (Fayette County, ~27 mi away), 35 MW (9/2026) -> 480 MW (9/2028) -> 1.5 GW (1/2031); AES Ohio's own project pages for the two Fayette customer feeds (OPSB 25-0742/25-0743-EL-BLN) attach it to 'the Jeffersonville, Ohio area' in its own words. A Dayton-market press ranking mislabelled it 'Wilmington' and this repo repeated the mislabel. Replace this bracket with the disclosed load the moment an instrument names THE CAMPUS's MW — the highest-value candidate is the OPSB filing for PJM's 'Customer Service Lines from Clinton 1 & 2' ($20M, two ~2-mile 345 kV feeds to an as-yet-unnamed customer substation, ISD 2028-12-31), whose affected-property table would name the served parcels. Full record: data/extracted/wilmington/data-centers.md. Discipline: this Clinton-County thread is SELF-CONTAINED — do NOT bridge the Lima/Allen Bistrozzi land-assembly graph.
disclosure_citation: Disclosed Nov 2025 via the joint Clinton County Port Authority / City of Wilmington Data Center FAQs [verified — chooseclintoncountyoh.org/news/data-center-faqs, wilmingtonohio.gov/data-center-faqs]: a ~471-acre campus on the former Cosler Farm at 1488 S US Route 68 (SW Wilmington), acquired by AWS in a PRIVATE transaction (not brokered by the Port Authority / City / JobsOhio); minimum 100 permanent jobs / ~$8M annual payroll. The $4B investment and the 9-building / 1,920,299 sq ft site plan are [reported — wnewsj 2025-12-03 'officials detail $4B AWS data center proposal'; WCPO]; a revised 12-building plan tabled 2026-03-27 is UNRECONCILED against the 9-building figure [open — resolve from the site-plan PDFs, #1470]. Legal posture (carried honestly): a federal court ordered the City to REDO three ordinances underpinning the campus — the data-center zoning-text amendment, the generator-noise exemption, and the Cosler Farm map rezoning — for defective public notice (Sharp v. City of Wilmington, S.D. Ohio 1:26-cv-00448, ruling ~2026-07-09/10 [reported — WCPO/WDTN/wnewsj converging]); the conditional-use ordinance O-26-33 has its final vote 2026-07-16. A proposed campus whose zoning basis is in remand is still a disclosed facility with pullable instruments, not a reason to zero the domain out. Ardent/TAC (a second ~545-ac rezoning corridor, O-26-04-07, 5-2 on 2026-02-19/20) is now structured as this site's SECOND facility (below), its investment / MW / instruments all [open]. See data/extracted/wilmington/data-centers.md.
cooling_model_citation: [reference] DIRECT EVAPORATIVE cooling disclosed in the joint Port Authority / City Data Center FAQs, with a projected ~6M gal/yr cooling-water CONSUMPTION and water-cooled operation only ~11 days/yr (dry/free-cooling otherwise) — mapped to the HYBRID_ADIABATIC archetype (dry with seasonal evaporative assist). The disclosed ~6M gal/yr at the screening IT load implies a very low water-use effectiveness (near-dry operation), which UNDERCUTS a large-abstraction premise — the water-thesis finding. Not a document extraction; the reserved withdrawal MGD, the Caesar Creek Lake source contract, and the WUE/back-solve reconciliation are the water plan (#1472). Wastewater returns to the City WWTP -> NPDES OH0028134 -> Lytle Creek -> Todd Fork -> Little Miami.
